g.text: Notes
Every vertical station is rim - k x D (k from the photos). The spec trio {rim
67.36, D 14.3, base-building roof 14.2} fails the photo-span / NAIP-ratio test
by ~3 m (buildings_tower.md 12.3) and is not a family: it is not drawn. Both
self-consistent families are drawn and neither is preferred: F1 D 15.2 m with
the rim at 221 ft (filled, levels right); F2 D 14.5 m, rim 64.0 m, 221 ft at
the mast tips (dash-dot outline, levels left). Station details (cab, slots,
seams, ribbon, blades) are drawn on F1 only.
CTBUH (Skyscraper Center, re-fetched 2026-11-04: "Structure Height 67.4 m /
221 ft, Floors 12") lists 221 ft as a height excluding antennae [pub, database
classification]: it favours F1's definition but is not a survey.
Settle with a surveyed ground photo (rim and grade), the NAIP shadow with the
flight time, or an SFO / FAA elevation drawing.
Round airside body: radius = A380-photo width ratios / 1.015 (the verification
found them ~1.5 % high) x D, so the flare is 1.58 D = the dimensioned value.
The cab is drawn on its inferred centre, offset 1.8 m (1.5 E, 1.0 N) from the
axis [inf]; 1.6 m in these views. Dark plinth ring under the cab glass, D 10.8
m (F1), from the flare deck to the sill [obs photo t1].
Slots (inf from photos t1 / t2, CC BY-SA 4.0): the upper band is discrete
slots, ~1.4 m wide, each sweeping ~20 deg of azimuth between the band seams
with its top towards the NNE (13 positions, none in the landside ribbon / wing
sector); the long slot is a helix sweeping ~44 deg (bearing 137 at its foot,
93 at its head). Drawn by projecting these plan bearings on the round body.
Landside (B): the ribbon sits in a flat-faced channel between a narrow, sharp
NE blade (pointed tip at about the flare rim) and a broad, louvred SW wing
with a rounded edge; both run full height with creases [obs, photos t3 / t4,
Famartin 2025, CC BY-SA 4.0]. Their proportions are read from oblique photos
[inf]; no source dimensions them. The ribbon faces bearing 310 (BT-01), so in
B it sits up to 2.3 m left of the axis; the SW wing tip (254 deg, 14.0 m in
plan) reproduces both oblique photos and projects inside the flare silhouette
from 297.7 deg.
Cab glazing: 24 panes of 6 x 11 ft [pub ENR] do not fit the drawn glass ring;
glazed arc 220 / 235 / 270 deg [pub, conflict]. Cab-glass lean 20 +-4 deg out
[obs]. Red obstruction light on the roof rim (SW) [obs, photo]; DOF lighting
code R [pub].
Cladding: ~1,500 curved trapezoidal ACM panels (4-mm Alucobond Plus "SFO
Silver") with spiralling joints [pub]. Drawn thin on F1: panel rows every 2.47
spec m (6 between the seams; the slot ends lie on rows) and ~68 helical joints
turning 2.6 deg of azimuth per spec metre, the twist of both slot kinds [rows
/ spacing obs photo t2; twist / count inf].
Flare top: a rounded shoulder rising inwards from the widest corner to the
plinth foot (t1: 0.35 m in the first 0.5 m, 0.86 m at 3.4 m, ~1.15 m at the
plinth) [obs photo t1]; the spec's vertical lip + flat deck is not drawn.
Not the base building: the tall dark louvred block seen beside the shaft (t1
left, t2 / t3 right) triangulates from the three photos to (-804, 259), 91 m
NW of the axis, the SE end of the Terminal 2 AirTrain station (SFO Museum
polygon); the thin canopy plates in t1 are that station's platform roof.
Neither is drawn.
